sources.text:
10 wk summer placement, Brightwater Analytics (small fintech), Manchester, Jun-Aug 2026
team: me + 2 platform engineers (Mateo, Jen)
- goal: move the nightly risk batch jobs off one big VM onto EKS so they stop blocking each other
- stack: Terraform, EKS, Karpenter, Argo Workflows, Prometheus, Loki
- decision: spot instances for the batch node pool, on-demand for the Argo controller. cheaper, jobs are retryable anyway
- problem: jobs randomly lost progress overnight, ~5% of runs. cause: spot interruptions + checkpoints only every 10 min
- investigated via node termination events in CloudWatch + the job logs. the 2 min warning wasn't enough
- fix: checkpoint every 90 s + a drain handler on the termination notice
- result: nightly run 4h10m -> 2h35m, nothing blocked since
- learned: read the spot termination docs first, not after
- why Graphcore: liked the scheduling side more than the models. want to work on the platform under the models
I wrote the Terraform modules for the node pools and the Karpenter autoscaler config myself, and Mateo reviewed them.

documents.text:
During a ten-week summer placement at Brightwater Analytics in Manchester, our three-person platform team moved the nightly risk batch jobs from a single virtual machine onto EKS. The nightly run improved from 4h10m to 2h35m, with nothing blocked since.

The main components were Terraform, EKS, Karpenter, Argo Workflows, Prometheus and Loki. The batch node pool used spot instances and the Argo controller used on-demand instances because this was cheaper and the jobs are retryable.

Jobs randomly lost progress overnight in ~5% of runs because of spot interruptions and checkpoints only every 10 minutes. Investigation used node termination events in CloudWatch and the job logs, and the 2 minute warning was not enough. The fix was to checkpoint every 90 seconds and add a drain handler on the termination notice. I learned to read the spot termination docs first, not after.

The team was me plus two platform engineers, Mateo and Jen. I wrote the Terraform modules for the node pools, Mateo wrote the Karpenter autoscaler config, and I reviewed his autoscaler change.

Dear Graphcore hiring team,

I am applying for the Graduate Cloud Platform Engineer 2027 role at Graphcore.

I liked the scheduling side more than the models, and I want to work on the platform under the models.

I did a 10 wk summer placement at Brightwater Analytics in Manchester, Jun-Aug 2026. My team was me plus 2 platform engineers, Mateo and Jen. The goal was to move the nightly risk batch jobs off one big VM onto EKS so they stop blocking each other. The stack included Terraform, EKS, Karpenter, Argo Workflows, Prometheus and Loki. I wrote the Terraform modules for the node pools, Mateo wrote the Karpenter autoscaler config, and I reviewed his autoscaler change. The decision was to use spot instances for the batch node pool and on-demand for the Argo controller, because it was cheaper and the jobs are retryable.

Jobs randomly lost progress overnight in ~5% of runs due to spot interruptions and checkpoints only every 10 min. The investigation used node termination events in CloudWatch and the job logs, and the 2 min warning was not enough. The fix was to checkpoint every 90 s plus a drain handler on the termination notice. The nightly run improved from 4h10m to 2h35m, with nothing blocked since. I learned to read the spot termination docs first, not after.

Thank you for considering my application.

Yours sincerely, Ellie
